title: Pay&Bill Administrator
description:
Pay & Bill Administrator

Working Pattern: Hybrid

The Opportunity

An established specialist provider of recruitment funding and back-office solutions is looking for an organised and detail-oriented Pay & Bill Administrator to join its growing team.

The business works closely with recruitment agencies, providing financial and administrative support across invoicing, contractor payments and payroll processes.

Reporting to the Operations Manager, you will be responsible for the day-to-day processing of pay and bill activities across a portfolio of recruitment agencies. This will include processing worker timesheets and payments, producing client invoices and ensuring all payroll and invoicing activities are completed accurately and on time.

You will work closely with recruitment agencies, workers and internal colleagues to ensure a smooth and efficient service, maintaining high standards of accuracy, communication and customer service.

Key Responsibilities
- Process timesheets received from recruitment agencies and arrange subsequent payments to workers across a variety of payment methods.
- Review agency payroll submissions, ensuring all information is accurate, complete and processed using the appropriate systems and technology.
- Ensure all worker payments are processed and delivered on time each week.
- Produce and issue client invoices in the required format, ensuring all relevant supporting documentation is included.
- Manage the weekly invoicing process, escalating any credit notes, invoice amendments or discrepancies to the appropriate senior team member.
- Ensure all pay and bill requests are supported by the correct documentation before processing.
- Proactively manage and resolve payroll queries, including worker payment queries, holiday pay, P45 requests and other payroll-related matters.
- Provide general administrative support, including data entry, filing, scanning and document management.
- Maintain accurate records and ensure all information is correctly recorded within company systems.
- Follow established guidelines, policies and procedures to ensure consistency, accuracy and best practice across all pay and bill activities.
- Build and maintain effective working relationships with recruitment agencies, workers and internal colleagues.

About You

Ideally, you will have previous experience within a pay and bill, payroll or recruitment administration environment.

Experience working for an umbrella company would also be highly advantageous, particularly with an understanding of PAYE, umbrella and CIS payroll processes.

We're looking for someone who is:
- Highly organised with excellent attention to detail.
- Comfortable working with figures, timesheets, invoices and payroll information.
- Confident using IT systems and handling data accurately.
- Proactive when dealing with queries and resolving issues.
- Able to manage deadlines and prioritise a varied workload.
- A confident communicator who enjoys building relationships with clients, workers and colleagues.
- A team player who takes pride in delivering an accurate and reliable service.

The Working Environment

You'll be joining a specialist team where accuracy, communication and consistency are key. The role offers a hybrid working arrangement, with three days in the office and two days working from home once fully trained.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with existing payroll, umbrella or recruitment administration experience to develop their career within the recruitment finance sector.

title: Lending Operations Administrator
description:
Lending Operations Administrator

Location: Chester City Centre (Fully Office Based)

Pay Rate: 13.34 per hour

Contract: Temporary Ongoing

Hours: Monday to Friday, 9:00am - 5:30pm

Are you an organised and detail-oriented operations professional with experience in financial services? We a Lending and Operations Administrator to join a busy and fast-paced operations team, supporting lending and asset finance activities within a highly regulated environment.

Working within a service-driven operations function, you will be responsible for completing operational checks, processing payments and payouts, ensuring documentation is accurate and compliant, and supporting the smooth activation of lending and asset finance facilities. You'll work closely with internal stakeholders and external brokers to deliver an excellent customer experience while meeting strict service level agreements.

Key Responsibilities
- Complete operational checks on lending and asset finance facilities prior to activation.
- Process payments, payouts and transfers accurately and within agreed SLAs.
- Ensure all documentation is complete, compliant and correctly executed.
- Liaise with internal teams and external brokers to progress deals efficiently.
- Manage operational inboxes and maintain accurate records and audit trails.
- Identify and escalate risks, exceptions or delays as required.
- Support process improvement initiatives and wider operational activities.

What We're Looking For

We are keen to speak with candidates who have experience within banking, lending, asset finance, mortgage administration, loan servicing or wider financial services operations.

The successful candidate will have:
- Previous experience working within a financial services environment.
- Strong attention to detail and a high level of accuracy.
- Experience following policies, procedures and compliance requirements.
- Excellent organisational and prioritisation skills.
- The ability to manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced, SLA-driven environment.
- Strong stakeholder management and communication skills.
- Confidence handling operational checks and high-value transactions.
- A proactive and professional approach to problem solving and service delivery.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with a background in lending operations, banking administration, asset finance operations, mortgage completions or loan servicing who is looking to join a well-established organisation and gain valuable experience within a busy financial services team.

title: Occupational Health Administrator
description:
Occupational Health Administrator Broughton, Nr Chester 12 Month contract 35 hours per week £17.92 ph paye Inside IR35

We currently have a requirement for an experienced administrator to provide support to a busy occupational health department , working with an aerospace client based in Broughton Near Chester
The Occupational Health department, has multiple clinicians across 2 UK site.and manages the
Health Surveillance programme, Sickness absence appointments and regular reviews (where required) for all UK employees.

This is a client-facing role, with the ability to converse with employees at all levels, across the company

Accountable for ensuring all Occupational Health communications are actioned appropriately, seek professional advice (where needed), ensuring follow on actions are implemented in a timely manner.

Using an Occupational Health Database (OrchidLive) to maintain the Occupational Health Diary, manage Occupational Health Reports processing, rescheduling appointments and scanning of documentation.

Proactively monitoring and updating required actions, enabling the Clinical Team to have the maximum information available to make informative decisions to support both employee and the business.

Interpret and appropriately action clinical instructions. This allows the clinical team to facilitate the maximum use of Occupational Health resource to ensure appropriate follow up appointments, referrals and treatment.

Facilitates appointments flow, action appropriate steps for any delays, with regular communication with employees, clinical staff and chief of positions (managers).

Be able to adhere to GDPR and medical confidentiality standards autonomously.

Working closely with the clinical team to ensure the smooth running of the multiple department clinics, with the ability to prioritise actions to meet customer & stakeholders expectations.

Skills required

Due to the nature of the department, dealing with sensitive information on a daily basis, confidentiality is of the utmost importance.

It is essential that you have previous experience of an office environment, work well as part of a team, you are flexible, adaptable, proactive and customer focused.

You must have a working knowledge of all Computer applications including Google Suite, Word, and Excel.

You will need to have the ability to multi-skill, prioritise tasks, use your initiative and work to tight deadlines.

Communication skills are essential, including the ability to deal with customers at all levels which could be face to face, via telephone or email.

Additional duties as the role develops
Preparation of daily/weekly/monthly and annual reports and KPIs for business to review/manage process adherence.

Liaising with claims officer, pensions officer and internal/external sub contracted clinical specialists.

Ability to support in sometimes, delicate and difficult situations/conversations, both with employees and their immediate families.

Further learned skills administration on Medical Database and Attendance Management System (AMS)

title: HR Administrator (12 months)
company: The Business Connection Group - Agency - Temporary
description:
Working for this business whose Chester Head Office is based in the city centre in a stunning location, the HR Administrator will be a 12-month maternity contract, working within a motivated, fast-paced and highly professional HR team. The HR Administrator will provide administrative support across the employee lifecycle, ensuring employee records, systems, documentation and payroll-related information are maintained accurately and confidentially.

Working Monday to Friday 9am-5pm, the HR Administrator role has benefits including free city centre parking; 25 days holiday plus Bank Holidays; an Employee Assistance Programme; employee recognition awards; and access to a platform with retail discounts and offers.

To apply for the HR Administrator role, you should be preferrably be CIPD level 3 qualified (or working towards this), with HR or relevant experience in a similar role.

Responsibilities:-

Provide administrative support across the employee lifecycle, ensuring employee records, systems, documentation and payroll-related information are maintained accurately, confidentially and in line with company policies, data protection requirements and relevant employment legislation.

Prepare and issue employee documentation including contracts, offer letters, contractual changes, family leave correspondence and leaver documentation.

Process and maintain information relating to new starters, leavers, employee changes, absence, benefits, pensions and other HR administration activities.

Prepare and maintain accurate payroll-related information, ensuring all updates are completed in line with monthly payroll deadlines.

Support recruitment administration including coordinating vacancies, arranging interviews, maintaining recruitment records and administering the Recruitment SharePoint site.

Prepare new starter and induction materials and co-ordinate onboarding activities.

Allocate training through the learning management system and maintain employee training records.

Record and maintain absence information on behalf of managers where required.

Produce routine HR reports and provide general administrative support to the wider HR team.

Skills and Experience:-

Previous experience in an HR administration, payroll administration, recruitment or similar is essential.

CIPD Level 3 qualification, or working towards this (desireable).

Strong organisational and time management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.

Able to work accurately under pressure and recognise when matters should be escalated to a more senior member of the HR team.

Good IT skills, including Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook and Teams. Experience of HR, payroll or learning management systems would be advantageous.

Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to build positive working relationships across the business.

Professional, approachable and trustworthy, with the ability to handle sensitive and confidential information appropriately.

Self-motivated, proactive and able to work independently while following established processes and procedures.

A collaborative team player who is willing to share knowledge, support colleagues and contribute to team objectives.

Strong attention to detail and commitment to maintaining accurate employee records, documentation and payroll-related information.

An understanding of the importance of GDPR, data protection requirements and confidentiality when handling employee information.
